title: Book Two · Chapter 111: Eighteen Names
story:
The first classroom is empty. Ronan stands at the door with a guide in his hand. He remembers the pupils outside the room on Wednesday. But he does not know most of their names.

He goes back to Miss Wu.

“How can I find all the copies?”

“How did you give them out?”

“Near the gate.”

“Did you keep a list?”

“No.”

She puts a sheet in front of him. “Begin with the pupils you know.”

Ronan writes the boy with the tree book. He cannot write a name, so he writes a short description instead. Then he remembers the boy with the long folder. Two pupils came together. One copy was for a brother.

He puts little squares beside the descriptions. There are eighteen copies outside the room. He has only six clear memories.

He looks at the first two descriptions again. He has written boy with a guide beside one square.

Nearly every pupil had a guide. That line will not help him find anyone.

He adds the long folder to the next description. He remembers the way it reached past the boy's elbow.

Then he looks toward the classroom door.

On Friday, faces moved past their table one after another. He was pleased to give the copies out. He did not stop to ask where each one would go.

Miss Wu waits while he adds a few more words.

“Do you know the class?”

“Not that one.”

“Then leave space. We can ask.”

Ronan moves the page closer. He planned to visit a few doors, change a few lines, and finish quickly.

Now the empty spaces on his list are part of the work too. He cannot put a tick beside a face he only half remembers.

Jun comes out with the leaf picture in a wide folder. He sees the list but walks toward his classroom.

Ronan wants to call him back. Jun knows the little boy's name. Jun can find him easily. Ronan takes one step, then stops.

Miss Wu asks a teacher for a few minutes with the younger pupils. She takes Ronan to the younger pupils' classroom. He stands at the front. The wrong time is on the board.

“Our guide says Wednesday,” he tells them. “The right time is Thursday after lunch. I copied an old time. I said I checked it with the teacher. I did not.”

A boy near the window lifts a guide.

“Do we give these back?”

“Please bring them to the table.”

Four guides arrive. Ronan puts a small paper strip across each wrong line. He writes the correct time clearly.

A girl says her guide is at home. Another pupil gave one to a sister in a different class.

Ronan writes those facts in his list. Miss Wu lets the pupils ask questions. He answers each one. He cannot finish in two minutes.

At the door, the boy with Jun's book stops him.

“Jun says the book can dry. I still made it wet.”

Ronan looks at him. “You did. But I gave you the wrong day. That is why you waited outside the closed room. You did not make that mistake.”

The boy presses his lips together and nods.

After school, Ronan carries four corrected copies back to the reading room. Four squares on his list have marks. The rest are empty.

Miss Wu gives him a little space on the board near the gate. He writes the correct time there. Under it he adds a request: PLEASE BRING YOUR GUIDE FOR A CORRECTION.

He makes the letters large. Pupils can read them from several steps away.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

description＝描述；strip＝纸条；request＝请求；memory＝记忆。

## 理解问题

1. Ronan为什么难以找到全部副本？
2. 他怎样向新生说明错误和谎言？

## 读句子

**Four guides / arrive.** 四份指南／被送来。
